transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Camille (Redwood Solutions), Priya (Halcyon Head of AI), Marco (Dir Eng), Lena (SRE), Omar (Procurement)

Auto-summary: (auto) focus on unit costs, expected token volumes (~200M tokens/mo), latency targets, and procurement next steps.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:08] Priya: Hi, Priya Desai. I run the AI team at Halcyon. We build customer-facing chat and autorespond features.
[00:12] Marco: Marco Ruiz, engineering lead, working on infra and scaling.
[00:15] Lena: Lena Park, SRE, focus on latency and cost ops.
[00:18] Omar: Omar Nadeem from procurement, will track timelines.
[00:21] Sofia: Great. Ethan and Camille from Redwood, we'll kickoff with high-level then jump into cost numbers.
[00:27] Ethan: Hi all. Quick ask: what's a realistic monthly budget and token volume you expect?
[00:33] Priya: We're planning for phase 1 100M tokens/month and expect this to grow to 200-250M within 3 months. Budget wise, roughly 30k-45k USD/month for inference. That's the sweet spot.
[00:47] Marco: Our p50/p95 targets are like <80ms p50 for chat, p95 <350ms if possible.
[00:55] Lena: Also need audit logs and retention, SSO, and key management — those are non-negotiable.
[01:02] Ethan: Got it. So two axes: unit cost (per-token) and latency SLOs. Hosted is easiest for start, Dedicated gives predictable unit economics via reserved capacity, Private for network isolation.
[01:16] Priya: Can you give example per-token numbers? We saw numbers from other vendors that vary a lot.
[01:22] Sofia: Sure — rough ballpark for hosted with a mid-size open LLM (similar to gpt-3.5 class) is about $0.0009 - $0.002 per token depending on batching and model variant. For large LLMs or low-latency configs it goes up. For dedicated reserved pools we can get effective per-token down to $0.0004 - $0.0007 with commitments because the infra cost is amortized. Those are examples, we'll run exact math for your workload.
[01:41] Marco: That delta matters. If we hit 200M tokens, at $0.001/token that's $200k — well outside budget. How do you get to our 30-45k?
[01:50] Ethan: Good callout. Two levers: batching (increasing tokens per batch reduces kernel overhead) and prefix/KV caching — for chat with many shared prefixes, caching reduces tokens evaluated. Also quantization/optimized kernels reduce per-token GPU time.
[02:05] Camille: To give a practical example: if you can batch to average 64 tokens per kernel step vs 8, the amortized compute goes down by ~4-6x depending on model. If you have a high cache hit rate (45-60%) for repeated prompts, that cuts downstream decode cost.
[02:22] Priya: Our workload has a lot of repeated templates — billing questions, status inquiries — so caching might help. But new prompt variants for personalization are common.
[02:31] Lena: From SRE standpoint, we can't tolerate cold-start latency spikes; how do dedicated pools handle burst capacity?
[02:37] Sofia: Dedicated can have reserved baseline plus burst capacity; bursts billed differently. You can configure autoscale policies and warm pools. Also we support local KV cache warmup strategies to avoid cold p99 spikes.
[02:51] Marco: Do you support prefix caching and partial KV reuse for multi-turn?
[02:55] Ethan: Yes — we have prefix/KV cache that stores key/value states, so repeated contexts avoid recomputation. It's model-specific and depends on how much of the session repeats.
[03:04] Priya: Can we quantify savings? ballpark for our mix (50% templated, 50% new) and 200M tokens raw?
[03:11] Camille: Rough calc: if 200M raw tokens with 50% cache hit at decode time, effective billed tokens could be ~140-160M depending on whether you cache prefixes before decoding. Combine batching benefits and quantized model performance you might hit effective cost near $0.0005/token which yields about $80k/month — still above your target. With a committed dedicated discount and aggressive batching we can approach $0.00025-0.00035/token => $50k-$70k/mo.
[03:39] Marco: So we'd need both a commitment and engineering work to batch more and tune caching. Is that realistic in 3 months?
[03:45] Priya: We can invest in batching libs and front-end changes but need to know ROI.
[03:50] Ethan: For ROI we propose a short benchmark: we run your sample workload on hosted first (no commitment) to measure base numbers, then provision a small dedicated pool and compare with same workload and batching knobs. We'll provide the cost model spreadsheet that shows per-token across scenarios.
[04:03] Omar: Procurement asks: if we go Dedicated, what's the billing cadence and cancellation terms?
[04:08] Sofia: Dedicated typically has monthly/annual commits; cancellation and change windows are defined in the contract — we'll share T&C. For pilots we can do a short-term reserved trial to prove economics.
[04:17] Priya: About private deployment — we have regulatory customers in EU, data residency matters. If we go Private, do you still provide control plane and security docs?
[04:26] Camille: Yes, Private gives customer-managed networking and optional on-prem. We still provide the control plane (optionally customer-hosted) with KMS integrations, audit logs, SSO, and SOC2 artifacts. Network/topology will affect cost though.
[04:38] Lena: We need to see SOC2 and network diagrams.
[04:40] Sofia: We'll share redwood-security.pdf and a sample network diagram link after the call.
[04:45] Priya: What about model licensing and quantization? We need to ensure output parity when using quantized variants.
[04:50] Ethan: Generally quantization (8-bit/4-bit) can slightly change outputs; we have quality checks and eval harness to compare. For critical flows we recommend running both and A/B comparing. Quantization often reduces costs 1.8-3x.
[04:59] Marco: Any hidden costs — egress, logging, tracing?
[05:03] Sofia: There can be add-ons: long-term observability retention, advanced tracing retention, or on-prem support lines. We'll call those out in the quote.
[05:11] Priya: Ok — what's typical timeline to get to a pilot?
[05:14] Sofia: If we get sample data and access this week, we can schedule the benchmark next week and have results within 5 business days. From there a pilot on Dedicated could start in 2-3 weeks, depending on procurement.
[05:23] Omar: That aligns with our Q2 priorities.
[05:26] Ethan: I'll outline the exact benchmark steps in the runbook; it will include token accounting, batch sizes, cache warmup procedure, and a script for replaying requests.
[05:36] Marco: One more question — for embeddings and reranking we have heavy throughput but smaller token sizes. Does batching help there too?
[05:43] Camille: Yes, batching embeddings yields big GPU utilization wins; you're typically charged per embedding unit and batching across requests reduces per-embedding cost significantly.
[05:50] Priya: Any reference numbers for embeddings?
[05:52] Sofia: For embeddings, hosted rates are per 1k embeddings; with batching and dedicated you can drop unit cost by 2-3x. We'll include examples in the spreadsheet.
[05:59] Lena: On SSO — we need SAML + SCIM for user provisioning.
[06:03] Sofia: Supported — we'll send the SSO guide.
[06:06] Priya: Great. For the benchmark, we will provide a 48-hour sample of anonymized traffic and label templates.
[06:12] Ethan: Perfect. We'll run the two scenarios and return numbers: hosted baseline, dedicated reserved with varying batch sizes, and dedicated with quantized models.
[06:20] Priya: Can you put a sample cost calc in the doc with breakouts? tokens, compute, infra, add-ons?
[06:25] Camille: Yes — the redwood_cost_model_v2.xlsx will have per-token calc, assumptions, and sensitivity toggles for cache hit rate and batch size.
[06:33] Marco: Any other technical risks we should flag? Memory blowups with large context lengths, and KV cache eviction patterns.
[06:38] Ethan: We'll surface memory/sparsity issues in the benchmark; also recommend sequence-length capping in latency-critical flows.
[06:45] Priya: Sounds good.
[06:47] Sofia: Quick recap of next steps: Sofia sends cost spreadsheet + security docs; Ethan prepares benchmark runbook and trigger; Priya shares sample data; Omar confirms procurement timeline.
[06:58] Omar: I'll confirm PO windows and share procurement namespace.
[07:02] Marco: Thanks all.
[07:04] Priya: Thanks.
[07:06] Sofia: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by Friday.

Notes / links referenced: cost model (redwood_cost_model_v2.xlsx), security pack (redwood-security.pdf), benchmark runbook (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/runbook-halcyon), sample script (link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/halcyon-sample-replay).

Transcript notes: transcription contains several minor mis-hearings (product names and acronyms), speaker attribution approximate.
